questions.question: A student burns a food sample to heat 50g of water. The temperature of the water rises by 10 °C. Using the formula: Energy (J) = mass of water (g) x rise in temperature (°C) x 4.2, how much energy was transferred to the water?
Which two measurements of a person are required to calculate their Body Mass Index (BMI)?
options: Height and waist circumference
Body mass and age
Height and body mass
Body mass and daily calorie intake

questions.question: How does physical fitness typically affect a person's recovery time after intense exercise?
options: Fitter individuals take a longer time for their heart rate to return to resting level.
Fitter individuals have a shorter recovery time.
Fitness has no measurable effect on recovery time.
Fitter individuals do not experience any increase in heart rate during exercise.

questions.question: What is the primary cause of a deficiency disease in humans?
options: Consuming too many calories from carbohydrates and fats.
Not consuming enough of a particular nutrient in the diet.
An infection caused by harmful bacteria in contaminated water.
A lack of regular physical exercise and sleep.

questions.question: In addition to acting as building blocks for growth, what is the primary role of food in cellular respiration?
options: To provide the fuel needed to release energy for life processes.
To directly transport oxygen from the lungs to the muscles.
To serve as a cooling agent to lower body temperature.
To eliminate waste products from the bloodstream.

questions.question: Why do breathing rate and heart rate increase during physical exercise?
options: To reduce the amount of water lost through sweat.
Because cells require more oxygen for cellular respiration to release energy.
To slow down the digestion of food in the stomach.
To prevent carbon dioxide from entering the lungs.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why nutritional requirements vary among individuals?
options: Everyone requires the exact same ratio of nutrients regardless of age.
Nutrients are only needed during early childhood and not in adulthood.
People need different amounts of particular nutrients depending on their life stage and lifestyle.
Dietary needs are determined solely by a person's height and nothing else.

questions.question: In a school laboratory experiment to compare the energy content of different foods, how is the energy released from burning food directly measured?
options: By measuring the mass of the ash left behind.
By measuring the temperature change of a known volume of water heated by the burning food.
By measuring the volume of oxygen consumed by the flame.
By measuring the time it takes for the food to stop burning.

questions.question: When investigating how different types of exercise affect heart rate, which of the following should be kept as control variables to ensure a fair test?
options: The starting heart rate and the final breathing rate.
The person performing the exercise and the length of time spent exercising.
The type of exercise and the room temperature.
The height of the participant and the time of day the results are plotted.

questions.question: Which two units are commonly used on nutritional labels to compare the amount of energy provided by different foods?
options: Kilograms and grams
Kilojoules and calories
Watts and joules per second
Degrees Celsius and Fahrenheit

questions.question: Which of the following health issues is a well-documented risk associated with obesity?
options: Scurvy
Heart disease
Iron-deficiency anemia
Color blindness

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'recovery time' in the context of physical exercise?
options: The duration of the exercise session itself.
The time it takes for the heart rate to return to its resting rate after exercise stops.
The total hours of sleep a person needs after an active day.
The time taken for breathing rate to double during a workout.

questions.question: How can changes in normal body appearance, function, or behaviour be classified in a medical context?
options: They are always signs of a healthy, adapting body.
They can be symptoms of ill health.
They are purely psychological and do not relate to physical health.
They indicate that a person is consuming too many vitamins.

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only recognized major food groups needed by the human body?
options: Protein, carbohydrate, lipids/fats, water, minerals, vitamins and fibre
Sugars, enzymes, hormones, water and calcium
Amino acids, glucose, starch, iron and oxygen
Protein, carbon, hydrogen, water and dietary supplements

questions.question: If you are drawing a bar chart to show how different categories of exercise affect heart rate, where should the 'amount of exercise' be placed?
options: On the y-axis, because it is continuous data.
On the x-axis, because it is categoric data representing the independent variable.
In a separate key, because it cannot be plotted on an axis.
On the x-axis, because it represents the dependent variable.
